title: Timed Mixed Lab Set A

header.html: All five domains (weighted like the exam: Troubleshooting 5 tasks, Cluster Architecture 4, Services and Networking 3, Workloads 2, Storage 2)
review of every domain under time pressure
Kubernetes v1.37.0; every task in this set was executed and validated in Modules 1 to 13 (setup, failing check, solution, passing check, wrong answers rejected)

html:
1How to use this set

  1. Reset: make sure the lab cluster is healthy (kubectl get nodes shows three Ready nodes).
  2. Start a 120-minute timer. Allowed documentation only: kubernetes.io/docs and blog, helm.sh/docs, gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io.
  3. For each task, prepare its starting state with python run_labs.py --setup <lab-id> (it also prints the task), then solve it as you would on the exam.
  4. Score yourself with python run_labs.py --check <lab-id>. A task is all-or-nothing, like the exam's scoring.
  5. Pass mark: 66% of the points.

Honest note: this set reuses tasks from the module labs, so you have seen their wording before. Use it as a timed rehearsal of speed and routine, then use the killer.sh simulator for tasks you have never seen.

2Tasks

<!-- SET: m12-01-kubelet-stopped,m11-03-fix-image-pull,m13-03-readiness-no-endpoints,m11-06-oomkilled,m12-05-scheduler-broken,m02-01-role-binding,m03-01-etcd-backup,m04-02-helm-upgrade-rollback,m02-04-fix-rolebinding,m07-02-nodeport-service,m09-02-allow-from-namespace,m08-04-fix-dns-down,m05-01-rollback-stuck-update,m06-05-node-affinity,m10-01-dynamic-pvc,m10-04-reclaim-retain -->

Set size: 16 tasks, 102 points in total. Pass mark: 66%, which is 68 points. Suggested time: 120 minutes (the labs' own time estimates add up to 102 minutes). Do the tasks in order, flag what you skip, and check your work as you would on the exam.

Task 1 (Troubleshooting, 7 points, about 6 minutes) m12-01-kubelet-stopped

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Node cka-worker shows NotReady. Find the cause and fix it so the node is Ready. The fix must survive a restart of the node (the kubelet service must be enabled and running). Hint: ssh cka-worker, then sudo -i; look at systemctl and journalctl.

Task 2 (Troubleshooting, 5 points, about 5 minutes) m11-03-fix-image-pull

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace app3, the Deployment web (2 replicas) shows ImagePullBackOff. Find the cause and fix the Deployment so that both replicas run nginx:alpine.

Task 3 (Troubleshooting, 7 points, about 7 minutes) m13-03-readiness-no-endpoints

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace net3, requests to http://shop.net3 fail although the Service shop selects the right Pods. The Pods are Running but not Ready. Find the cause and fix the Deployment shop (do not change the Service) so that http://shop.net3 returns the nginx welcome page.

Task 4 (Troubleshooting, 7 points, about 7 minutes) m11-06-oomkilled

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace app6, the Pod hungry restarts all the time. Find the reason in the Pod's status. The container needs about 40 MiB of memory to run. Recreate the Pod hungry (same image and command) with a memory limit of 128Mi so that it runs stably with 0 restarts.

Task 5 (Troubleshooting, 8 points, about 9 minutes) m12-05-scheduler-broken

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

New Pods in the namespace sched1 stay Pending with no node assigned (the Deployment probe-app has 2 replicas). Existing workloads are fine. Find the faulty control plane component on cka-control-plane and repair it so that both Pods are scheduled and become Ready.

Task 6 (Architecture, 5 points, about 5 minutes) m02-01-role-binding

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace dev, create a Role pod-reader that allows the verbs get, list and watch on Pods only. Bind it with a RoleBinding named read-pods to the user jane. The user must not be able to delete Pods, and must not be able to read Pods in other namespaces.

Task 7 (Architecture, 7 points, about 6 minutes) m03-01-etcd-backup

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

On the control plane node cka-control-plane, take a snapshot of etcd and save it as /opt/backup/etcd.db. Find the endpoint and the certificate paths in the etcd static Pod manifest. etcdctl is installed on the node.

Task 8 (Architecture, 7 points, about 7 minutes) m04-02-helm-upgrade-rollback

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The release app (chart ~/charts/webapp) is installed in the namespace helm-ns with 1 replica. First upgrade the release so that it runs 3 replicas. Then the change turns out to be a mistake: roll the release back to its first revision. At the end the release must run 1 replica and the history must show the upgrade and the rollback.

Task 9 (Troubleshooting, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m02-04-fix-rolebinding

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace shop2, the ServiceAccount app cannot read ConfigMaps although a Role and a RoleBinding exist. Find the mistake and fix it so that app can get and list ConfigMaps in shop2 (and nothing outside that namespace). Keep the Role named cm-reader and the RoleBinding named app-cm. Hint: some fields of a RoleBinding cannot be edited; you may need to recreate it.

Task 10 (Networking, 5 points, about 5 minutes) m07-02-nodeport-service

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace svc2, expose the Deployment web (nginx on port 80) with a Service named web-np of type NodePort, service port 80, using the fixed node port 30080.

Task 11 (Networking, 7 points, about 8 minutes) m09-02-allow-from-namespace

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace np2, the Pod api (nginx, port 80) must accept TCP traffic on port 80 only from Pods in namespaces that carry the label team=frontend. Everything else must be denied. The namespace fe has the label team=frontend and the namespace other does not. Create one NetworkPolicy named api-from-frontend in np2.

Task 12 (Troubleshooting, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m08-04-fix-dns-down

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Name resolution inside the cluster has stopped: Pods cannot resolve kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local. Find out why and fix it so that name resolution works again and CoreDNS runs with its normal 2 replicas.

Task 13 (Workloads, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m05-01-rollback-stuck-update

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace roll, the Deployment web (3 replicas) was updated to an image tag that does not exist, and the update is stuck. Roll the Deployment back to the previous working revision and make sure all 3 replicas are Ready.

Task 14 (Workloads, 7 points, about 7 minutes) m06-05-node-affinity

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The node cka-worker carries the label tier=gold. In the namespace aff, create a Deployment gold-app with 3 replicas of nginx:alpine that must be scheduled only on nodes whose label tier is gold. Use node affinity (requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution), not nodeSelector.

Task 15 (Storage, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m10-01-dynamic-pvc

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st1, create a PersistentVolumeClaim data requesting 1Gi with access mode ReadWriteOnce, using the cluster's default StorageClass. Then create a Pod writer (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that mounts the claim at /data and write the text hello to the file /data/test.txt in that Pod.

Task 16 (Storage, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m10-04-reclaim-retain

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st4, the PersistentVolumeClaim keepme is bound to a dynamically provisioned PersistentVolume whose reclaim policy is Delete. The data must survive even if the claim is deleted. Change the reclaim policy of that PersistentVolume to Retain. Do not change the claim or the StorageClass.

<!-- /SET -->

3Reference solutions

Open these only after the timer ends.

<!-- SETSOL: m12-01-kubelet-stopped,m11-03-fix-image-pull,m13-03-readiness-no-endpoints,m11-06-oomkilled,m12-05-scheduler-broken,m02-01-role-binding,m03-01-etcd-backup,m04-02-helm-upgrade-rollback,m02-04-fix-rolebinding,m07-02-nodeport-service,m09-02-allow-from-namespace,m08-04-fix-dns-down,m05-01-rollback-stuck-update,m06-05-node-affinity,m10-01-dynamic-pvc,m10-04-reclaim-retain -->

Solution 1: m12-01-kubelet-stopped

ssh cka-worker 'systemctl status kubelet --no-pager | head -5'
ssh cka-worker 'systemctl enable --now kubelet'
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/cka-worker --timeout=120s

Solution 2: m11-03-fix-image-pull

kubectl -n app3 describe pod -l app=web | grep -i -A3 "Failed to pull" | head -6
kubectl -n app3 set image deployment web nginx=nginx:alpine
kubectl -n app3 rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

Solution 3: m13-03-readiness-no-endpoints

kubectl -n net3 get pods
kubectl -n net3 describe pod -l app=shop | grep -i -A2 "Readiness probe failed" | head -4
kubectl -n net3 patch deployment shop --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/"}]'
kubectl -n net3 rollout status deployment shop --timeout=120s

Solution 4: m11-06-oomkilled

kubectl -n app6 get pod hungry -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].lastState.terminated.reason}'; echo
kubectl -n app6 delete pod hungry --force --grace-period 0
kubectl -n app6 apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: hungry}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "x=$(yes | head -c 40000000); echo allocated; sleep 3600"]
    resources:
      limits: {memory: 128Mi}
Y
kubectl -n app6 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/hungry --timeout=120s
sleep 15

Solution 5: m12-05-scheduler-broken

ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl ps -a --name kube-scheduler'
ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl logs $(crictl ps -a --name kube-scheduler -q | head -1) 2>&1 | tail -3'
ssh cka-control-plane 'sed -i "s#scheduler.cnf#scheduler.conf#" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane 'systemctl restart kubelet'   # resets the crash-loop back-off of the static Pod
kubectl -n sched1 rollout status deployment probe-app --timeout=180s

Solution 6: m02-01-role-binding

kubectl -n dev create role pod-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods
kubectl -n dev create rolebinding read-pods --role=pod-reader --user=jane

Solution 7: m03-01-etcd-backup

ssh cka-control-plane 'grep -E "cert-file|key-file|trusted-ca-file|listen-client" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane 'etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key snapshot save /opt/backup/etcd.db'

Solution 8: m04-02-helm-upgrade-rollback

helm upgrade app ~/charts/webapp -n helm-ns --set replicaCount=3 --wait --timeout 120s
helm history app -n helm-ns
helm rollback app 1 -n helm-ns --wait --timeout 120s
helm history app -n helm-ns

Solution 9: m02-04-fix-rolebinding

kubectl -n shop2 get rolebinding app-cm -o yaml | grep -A3 roleRef
kubectl -n shop2 delete rolebinding app-cm
kubectl -n shop2 create rolebinding app-cm --role=cm-reader --serviceaccount=shop2:app

Solution 10: m07-02-nodeport-service

kubectl -n svc2 expose deployment web --name=web-np --port=80 --type=NodePort --dry-run=client -o yaml > /tmp/web-np.yaml
sed -i 's/  - port: 80/  - port: 80\n    nodePort: 30080/' /tmp/web-np.yaml
kubectl -n svc2 apply -f /tmp/web-np.yaml
kubectl -n svc2 get svc web-np

Solution 11: m09-02-allow-from-namespace

kubectl -n np2 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: api-from-frontend}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: api}}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {team: frontend}}
    ports:
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 80}
Y
sleep 5

Solution 12: m08-04-fix-dns-down

kubectl -n kube-system get deployment coredns
kubectl -n kube-system get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=kube-dns
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment coredns --replicas=2
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deployment coredns --timeout=120s

Solution 13: m05-01-rollback-stuck-update

kubectl -n roll rollout history deployment web
kubectl -n roll rollout undo deployment web
kubectl -n roll rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

Solution 14: m06-05-node-affinity

kubectl -n aff apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: gold-app}
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: gold-app}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: gold-app}}
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
            - matchExpressions:
              - {key: tier, operator: In, values: [gold]}
      containers:
      - {name: web, image: "nginx:alpine"}
Y
kubectl -n aff rollout status deployment gold-app --timeout=120s
kubectl -n aff get pods -o wide

Solution 15: m10-01-dynamic-pvc

kubectl -n st1 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: data}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: writer}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: vol, mountPath: /data}
  volumes:
  - name: vol
    persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: data}
Y
kubectl -n st1 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/writer --timeout=120s
kubectl -n st1 exec writer -- sh -c 'echo hello > /data/test.txt'
kubectl -n st1 get pvc data

Solution 16: m10-04-reclaim-retain

pv=$(kubectl -n st4 get pvc keepme -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumeName}')
kubectl get pv $pv
kubectl patch pv $pv -p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}'
kubectl get pv $pv

<!-- /SETSOL -->

4Review after the set

  1. Which tasks went over 8 minutes? Redo them cold the next day.
  2. Which mistakes were reading mistakes (namespace, name, context)? Add them to your personal checklist.
  3. Did you verify each task with a second command?

5Recall questions

R1Which domain should get the most tasks in a practice set and why?

Show the answer

Troubleshooting, because it carries 30% of the score.

R2What is the pass mark for this set?

Show the answer

66% of the points.

R3What do you do with a task that takes more than about 6 minutes?

Show the answer

Flag it, move on, and return at the end.

R4What is scored in each task: your commands or the final state?

Show the answer

The final cluster state.

R5Why verify with a second command?

Show the answer

Typos in names, namespaces and ports are the most common cause of lost tasks.

R6Where can you practice tasks you have never seen?

Show the answer

In the killer.sh simulator included with the exam registration.
